scope: The one component figure and this audit only; no registry, course, lesson, corpus, receiver, evidence, or other figure file was edited.
teaching_claim: A fair receiver audit fixes the coordinate set before comparing algorithms, preserves each arithmetic unit, keeps source and received-signal timing origins separate, and reports the separate implemented receiver's failed targets beside its passed targets.

implementation.root: div with role=img; no nested figure or figcaption element
implementation.layout: An exact-coordinate group containing two method cards is separated by a literal not-equal marker from one N=256 FFT-grid card; two timing rails and a hard-divided N=160 study ledger follow below.
implementation.responsive: At widths at or below 650 px, all cost cards, timing rails, and study rows stack. The two exact-frequency sets wrap independently so no KaTeX token crosses its card.

palette_roles.amber: N=205 exact physical-frequency coordinate family and received-origin duration rail
palette_roles.blue: different N=256 FFT-grid coordinate family and source-to-received FIR-delay rail
palette_roles.currentColor_dashed: measured target FAIL rows and unit-neutral scaffold

n205_exact_goertzel.coordinates: the same eight physical frequencies, including possibly noninteger resonator coordinates

n256_selected_direct.coordinates: eight selected X_256[k_i] FFT-grid coordinates over 205 acquired samples plus 51 zeros

n256_radix2_fft.guardrail: 1024 is labeled twiddle slots, never total operations.

coordinate_and_operation_contract.unit_guardrail: No real multiplication, real addition, complex product slot, complex addition, or twiddle slot is added to a heterogeneous total, and no algorithm winner is claimed.

latency_contract.received_origin_rail: received-signal origin to named duration qualification: 320 received samples =40 ms; actual decision latency requires the declared 5 ms block/hop schedule
latency_contract.source_origin_rail: source origin through the synthetic 101-tap FIR to received-signal origin: 50 samples =6.25 ms
latency_contract.guardrail: The two values occupy separate rails. The figure does not print 46.25 ms or another fabricated universal end-to-end total.

separate_receiver_study.label: separate frozen N=160 receiver study with 5 ms temporal blocks
separate_receiver_study.coordinate_note: The study uses a 160-sample, 20 ms exact-nominal spectral record; it is not attributed to the N=205 or N=256 cost alternatives above.

rows.metric: held-out 10 dB active-tone-SNR with independent +/-1.5% offsets
maximum accepted hard-set latency from received-signal onset

separate_receiver_study.denominator_guardrail: Training and all 24-39 ms gray-region trials are visibly excluded; the ledger is labeled a deterministic synthetic course study, not standards conformance.

defects_seen: The desktop grid stretched the shorter exact-coordinate group to the taller N=256 card, leaving excess framed whitespace.
At 312 px the single unbreakable KaTeX set of all eight exact frequencies crossed the amber group border.
render_loop.fix: Top-aligned the coordinate groups and split the exact low/high frequency sets into independently wrapping KaTeX tokens.

render_loop.verdict: PASS: all coordinate labels, operation units, timing origins, observed denominators, targets, signs, and PASS/FAIL words remain legible without collision or clipping.

integration_handoff.registry_entry: DtmfCoordinateCostLatencyLedger using the repository's existing figure registry pattern
integration_handoff.embed: <Figure name="DtmfCoordinateCostLatencyLedger" alt="A ledger compares exact 205-sample correlation and Goertzel costs with a 256-point FFT-grid cost, separates 40 milliseconds from received onset from the FIR's 6.25-millisecond source delay, and audits a separate 160-sample receiver study: clean and 10-decibel accuracy pass, while negative-control rejection and a 50-millisecond hard-set maximum latency fail their targets." caption="A fair comparison fixes coordinates, units, and latency origin; the frozen study passes two targets and exposes two failures." />
